title: UI-MOPD: Teaching One GUI Agent Many Platforms Without Forgetting
hook: Train a GUI agent on a new platform and it often forgets the old ones. UI-MOPD picks a different teacher per platform on the fly, so cross-platform learning stops fighting itself.
key_points: Cross-platform GUI agents struggle because platforms differ in interaction conventions — joint training tends to mix behaviors, degrade platform-specific skill, or cause catastrophic forgetting.
UI-MOPD is the first method to bring multi-teacher on-policy distillation into continual learning for GUI agents.
It dynamically selects a platform-specific teacher based on the current environment, transferring that platform's behavioral priors into one shared policy via platform-conditioned distillation.
This lets the shared policy adapt to a new platform while preserving what it already learned on others.
Paired with a new cross-platform dataset (Uni-GUI); on OSWorld and MobileWorld the method reaches 38.2% and 12.0% task success respectively.
content_html: Building one GUI agent that works across desktop, mobile, and web is harder than it sounds: each platform has its own interaction conventions, and training on all of them at once tends to blur behaviors or wipe out skills the agent already had. UI-MOPD is a new fix aimed squarely at that problem.
extra_html: Niu Lian and colleagues introduce UI-MOPD, described as the first method to bring multi-teacher on-policy distillation into continual learning for GUI agents. Instead of a single fixed teacher, it dynamically selects a platform-specific teacher based on the agent's current environment, then transfers that platform's behavioral priors into one shared policy through platform-conditioned distillation — letting the agent pick up a new platform without erasing what it learned on prior ones. The team also built Uni-GUI, a cross-platform interaction dataset, to support training. On the OSWorld and MobileWorld benchmarks, the resulting agent reaches 38.2% and 12.0% task success respectively.

related.title: GUI vs. CLI: Where Computer-Use Agents Get Stuck
related.hook: Should an agent click buttons or type commands? A matched benchmark giving both the same 440 tasks finds GUI agents win by default — but CLI agents leap ahead once their skill library is filled in.

related.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation isn't a midpoint between fine-tuning and RL — it carves its own narrow path through parameter space, locking into a low-dimensional subspace early in training.

related.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation breaks when teacher and student disagree too much. TrOPD only trusts the teacher where its supervision is reliable — and skips the rest.

flashcards.prompt: What continual-learning problem does UI-MOPD target in GUI agents?
flashcards.back_html: Training one agent across multiple platforms (with different interaction conventions) tends to cause behavioral mixing, platform-specific skill loss, or catastrophic forgetting of older platforms.

flashcards.prompt: How does UI-MOPD avoid forgetting older platforms while learning a new one?

choices.text: It dynamically picks a platform-specific teacher for the current environment and distills its behavior into a shared policy via platform-conditioned distillation
It trains a completely separate model for every platform
It replays all past interaction logs verbatim during every new training run

flashcards.explanation_html: Rather than one fixed teacher or isolated per-platform models, UI-MOPD's teacher choice adapts to the current platform, letting one shared policy absorb each platform's behavioral priors without overwriting the others.

flashcards.prompt: What are UI-MOPD's task success rates on OSWorld and MobileWorld?
flashcards.back_html: 38.2% on OSWorld and 12.0% on MobileWorld — reported as evidence it balances retaining old-platform capability with adapting to a new one.
